display.title: A Tzaddik's Brachah: Why a Blessing Is Like Rain
display.summary_short: Hashem gave Avraham Avinu and the tzaddikim the power to bless. Like rain on plowed soil, a brachah takes hold only when we prepare ourselves with mitzvos.
display.summary_long: A short teaching from the Tzivos Hashem radio show that introduces the story 'The Blessing of a Tzaddik'. Uncle Yossi explains that Hashem gave the very first Jew, Avraham Avinu, a special power: whomever he blessed, Hashem would bless too. That is the meaning of 'and you shall be a blessing', which Rashi explains as 'the blessings are placed in your hand'. The gift passed to Yitzchak and Yaakov, and in every generation Hashem grants it to the tzaddikim. Our Sages compare a tzaddik's brachah to rain. Rain only makes things grow when the soil has been cleared of stones and plowed soft, ready for seeds. In the same way, to receive a brachah in full we must prepare ourselves and remove what is in the way: aveiros block a brachah, while mitzvos act like powerful magnets that draw Heavenly blessing. The clip ends just as the story is about to begin.
display.lesson: Prepare yourself with mitzvos to receive blessing, the way a farmer prepares soil for the rain.
